Ethical Considerations Generative AI use at West Chester University should adhere to ethical principles, including privacy, fairness, transparency, and accountability. Researchers and users should consider the potential societal impacts of AI technologies, such as fairness, bias, and privacy. Data Privacy and Security Users must follow data privacy and security guidelines when using generative AI, protecting personal and institutional data. Faculty Use generative AI to enhance teaching and learning experiences while maintaining academic integrity. Be transparent about the use of AI-generated content in course materials. Encourage students to use AI responsibly and ethically. Learn more about Teaching with Generative AI Staff Use generative AI to improve administrative processes and decision-making. units.passage: Small, everyday uses do not count. Spellcheck, grammar underlining, and short autocomplete suggestions of a few words that are built into the word-processing or document-creation software in which the work is produced (e.g., Microsoft Word, Google Docs, or Apple Pages), AI summaries that appear on their own in search results, and assistive technology used under a documented accommodation do not count as AI use at any level. Your professor may restrict one of these only when it is central to what the assignment measures (for example, spelling in a language course), and they must say so explicitly.
units.why: "Spellcheck, grammar underlining, and short autocomplete suggestions... do not count as AI use at any level" exempts routine embedded features (P100).

units.passage: Your professor may restrict one of these only when it is central to what the assignment measures (for example, spelling in a language course), and they must say so explicitly.

units.passage: Uses that do not count as AI use at any level of this policy: spellcheck and grammar underlining, autocomplete of a few words, AI-generated summaries that appear unsolicited in search results, and AI-based assistive technology used under a documented accommodation. units.passage: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools may be used in this course so long as you 1. Acknowledge when and how you used them a. Include the name of the tool and a brief description of what you did. Examples of how to do this in different scenarios are at the bottom of the WCU Generative AI Guiding Framework. b. When in doubt, err on the side of acknowledgment. c. Proper acknowledgment ensures academic integrity and demonstrates understanding of the source and influence of generative AI tools on your work. 2. Verify the accuracy of AI outputs a. You are responsible for what you submit under your name, even if you used AI to create part or all of it. b. Be cautious about using AI answers regarding subjects you do not know well. AI tools make mistakes that appear accurate to novices in the subject. c. Don’t assume AI tools are using accurate sources. You need to double check that the sources are real and say what AI says they say. If I suspect you used Generative AI and you did not acknowledge that use, I reserve the right to withhold a grade until I have had a conversation with you. Use with Permission Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools may be used for specific assignments with prior permission.
